title: Did Thumbs Down Really Mean Death for Gladiators? #shorts
description:
The emperor's thumbs down is the most famous gesture in Roman history — and nobody knows if it's real.

Roman writers say the crowd "turned the thumb" (pollice verso) but never say which way. It may have been up or sideways; some think a hidden thumb meant mercy. The thumbs-down image comes from Jean-Léon Gérôme's 1872 painting Pollice Verso, which films later copied. Also: most gladiator fights didn't end in death — trained fighters were expensive, and many fought again.

Animated, voiced and scored in code. Narration is a synthetic (text-to-speech) voice.

title: Nobody Was Burned at the Salem Witch Trials #shorts
description:
Salem, 1692: witches burned at the stake. Except nobody was burned.

More than 200 people were accused, and courts accepted "spectral evidence" — basically dreams and visions. Nineteen people were executed by hanging, because under English law witchcraft was a felony, and felons were hanged. Giles Corey was pressed to death after refusing to plead, and others died in jail. Burning was mostly a continental European practice. Jurors later apologised, and in 2022 the last accused, Elizabeth Johnson Jr., was formally exonerated.

title: You Can't See the Great Wall From Space #shorts
description:
The Great Wall of China is thousands of miles long — but only a few metres wide, and about the same colour as the land around it. From orbit, spotting it with your eyes is like spotting a hair from miles away. China's first astronaut, Yang Liwei, said in 2003 that he couldn't see it. The claim is older than spaceflight: a 1932 cartoon said it could be seen from the Moon, where you can barely make out continents. With a zoom lens, maybe. With your eyes, no.

title: Cleopatra Lived Closer to the Moon Landing Than the Pyramids #shorts
description:
The Great Pyramid was built around 2560 BC. Cleopatra died in 30 BC — more than 2,500 years later. The Moon landing was in 1969, about 2,000 years after her. So Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.

Also: her family, the Ptolemies, were Greek and had ruled Egypt for nearly 300 years. Ancient writers say she was the first of them to learn Egyptian, and that she spoke about nine languages.
